hints: Count unordered node pairs whose distance is exactly k.
At a node, combine nodes in different child subtrees whose depths sum to k.
Process children one at a time, querying depths against previously processed children before adding the current child's counts.
analogy: At each node, pair each child's depth counts only with children already visited, so no pair is counted twice.
example: For k=2, two child nodes of the same center form one pair at distance 2.
algorithm: Use small-to-large map merging or a depth-frequency array per DFS. For each child depth d, add countSeen[k-d] to answer, then merge that child's counts upward.
correctness: Every pair has one LCA; its endpoints are in different child subtrees or one endpoint is the LCA, and the query-before-merge rule counts that pair at exactly that node once.
complexity: O(n log n) typical with small-to-large merging; O(n) auxiliary space.
